FROMGIT: PM / OPP: Introduce a power estimation helper The Energy Model (EM) framework provides an API to let drivers register the active power of CPUs. The drivers are expected to provide a callback method which estimates the power consumed by a CPU at each available performance levels. How exactly this should be implemented, however, depends on the platform. On some systems, PM_OPP knows the voltage and frequency at which CPUs can run. When coupled with the CPU 'capacitance' (as provided by the 'dynamic-power-coefficient' devicetree binding), it is possible to estimate the dynamic power consumption of a CPU as P = C * V^2 * f, with C its capacitance and V and f respectively the voltage and frequency of the OPP. The Intelligent Power Allocator (IPA) thermal governor already implements that estimation method, in the thermal framework. However, this power estimation method can be applied to any platform where all the parameters are known (C, V and f), and not only those suffering thermal issues. As such, the code implementing this feature can be re-used to also populate the EM framework now used by EAS. As a first step, introduce in PM_OPP a helper function which CPUFreq drivers can use to register into the EM framework. This duplicates the power estimation done in IPA until it can be migrated to using the EM framework. This will be done later, once the EM framework has support for at least all platforms currently supported by IPA. Signed-off-by: Quentin Perret <quentin.perret@arm.com> Tested-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Viresh Kumar <viresh.kumar@linaro.org> (cherry picked from commit a4f342b9607d8c2034d3135cbbb11b4028be3678 git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/vireshk/pm.git opp/linux-next) BUG=b:111527336, b:116109744 TEST=build for cheza Change-Id: I841b5e50ef057ca37d7ee8f20a0515209d909b3e Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1455078 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Evan Green <evgreen@chromium.org>

bluetooth: add suspend/resume infrastructure per powerd guidelines This CL extends the suspend_manager.cc in btdispatch to support a generic interface of BlueZ and NewBlue with the powerd, required for the system operations of suspend and resume. The dispatcher relays powerd notifications to BlueZ and to NewBlue, for them to perform any task needed prior suspend or after resume, and acknowledge back to powerd when both are done. New D-Bus messages were defined for the interaction between the dispatcher and BlueZ. No support is added for NewBlue in this change, however the generic infra in the btdispatcher can be extended to NewBlue in the future (b:123933149) Refer to b:123932305 for url of powerd guidelines. BUG=b:123932305 TEST=suspend and resume of system when discovery is running/not running Follow powerd logs to verify correct states. repeatable attempts to verify stability. Verify suspend and resume of discovery when UI tries to connect still working as before. arc-setup: Correct for subshell in arc-ureadahead arc-ureadahead attempts to exit early if its pack file is successfully read by ureadahead. When the script was migrated to use logger, the commands were moved into a compound group. Because the compound group is piped to logger, it is run in a subshell, so the exit doesn't have any effect on the parent shell. This means that the fallback arc-setup command is always run. The commands in the group always remove the packfile if it isn't valid, so instead of assuming that an early exit happens, we can just check for the pack file before running arc-setup. If it's still there, it must have been valid; if not, we need to run the fallback. BUG=chromium:930144 TEST=arc-setup --mode=read-ahead isn't run when pack file exists Change-Id: Ia21c4f45f3ba0a755b50aac9ddcda7a18ef98718 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1460341 Commit-Ready: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Tested-by: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org>

cups: Fix for PPD generation in lpadmin (missing IPP parameters) The problem occurs for some IPP Everywhere printers. For this kind of printers CUPS prepares PPD file basing on IPP parameters obtained from the printer. In the previous CUPS version (shipped with R71) IPP request sent to the printer does not have parameter requested-attributes. As a result, printers returned always full list of supported paramneters. In current CUPS version (R72) the request contains the parameter requested-attributes, what allows to reduce the size of expected response. Unfortunately, some printers cannot handle this parameter correctly and return incomplete responses. This patch solves this problem by removing the requested-attributes parameter from the request. BUG=chromium:929798 TEST=Tested on nautilus and printer Kodak Verite 55 EcoPlus (printing works) Change-Id: Icc77b3255b3958de4916b4593bb9f1365bce270d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1460143 Commit-Ready: Piotr Pawliczek <pawliczek@chromium.org> Tested-by: Piotr Pawliczek <pawliczek@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Kau <skau@chromium.org>

shill: routing: Add RemoveRoute and {Add,Remove}RouteRaw methods Prior to this change, the RoutingTable public API only allowed clients to add routes to a table, not to remove them. Internal code to remove routes from a table was done by manually calling ApplyRoute. This change introduces a RemoveRoute method and adds *Raw methods which allow for the addition/removal of routes without modifying the internal table bookkeeping. This is particularly useful when replacing routes or when dealing with routes that were added outside of shill (and hence might not yet have any bookkeeping information).
